status: Exploratory adversarial review; prior outcomes have been seen
authorization: The user requests a deep adversarial re-examination, a visual catalogue of the strongest new meanings with Sanskrit anchors and inscription examples, repository cleanup and public release, unattended.
new_information: The previous construction exercise did not compare competing semantic interpretations, correct its automatic priority rule, measure anchor-search multiplicity, or examine the consequences of missing graphic agreement. This review adds those analyses and incorporates the completed two-coder PDF audit without rerunning its frozen tests.
shared_assumptions: Reading direction follows the declared complete RTL single-line frame; sequences, faces, families and sites have separate denominators.
Sanskrit is a comparison vocabulary, with exact lexical matches distinguished from normalized matches and from broad functional interpretations.
The graph-to-meaning relationship and any full-stem insertion remain hypotheses. A dictionary attestation cannot independently verify an assigned graphic meaning.
No new archaeological sample or blinded independent semantic annotator is available in this run. Adversarial review is conducted by the same research agent with explicit rival predictions.
tests: Recount the old priorities and inspect whether their rule rewards frequency without evidential independence.
Audit every new anchor and recurring new proposal against actual drawings, placement, distinct contexts, object-family and site support.
Measure positional enrichment against length- and site-stratified within-text permutations, controlling the family of 17 original anchor codes; report effect sizes and multiple-testing correction.
Compare context substitution, adjacency, enclosure and added-stroke hypotheses with explicit rivals; retain functional conclusions when semantics do not separate.

For the three post-outcome lexical refinements and any shortlisted extensions, enumerate exact Sanskrit alternatives, anchor-word sensitivities, cross-context intersections, and frequency-matched/random-word negative controls. Treat post-selection diagnostics as diagnostics.
Check dictionary senses, compounds, attestation periods and sound versus meaning with primary dictionary and archaeological sources.
Use the two-coder graphic audit to expose disjoint or ambiguous crosswalks instead of silently importing one coder's sound values.
Build a separate catalogue with revised meanings, Sanskrit comparisons, selected attributed inscription windows, objections and exact result links. Preserve the full earlier catalogue unchanged.
selection: Prioritize repeatable graphic functions and human/tool composites. Prefer fewer well-supported semantic families over a forced specific meaning for every graphic code. No numerical probability of historical correctness is assigned.
storage: Full corpora, source font drawings, PDF crops, complete lexical search witnesses, detailed permutations and local history backups remain under data/raw/. Public outputs contain original analysis, aggregates, selected short attributed examples and CC BY chart representatives.
completion: Adversarial outcomes, revised catalogue, source and verification records, retrospective, a reviewed public Git payload and verified public repository visibility. No CI/CD or recurring automation.
